claims.quote: Concomitant potassium-containing salt substitutes should also not be used.
claims.locator: Contraindications › Antikaliuretic Therapy and Potassium Supplementation

claims.text: potassium supplements only for severe hypokalemia, with careful K monitoring.
claims.quote: Potassium supplementation should not be used with triamterene and hydrochlorothiazide except in severe cases of hypokalemia. Such concomitant therapy can be associated with rapid increases in serum potassium levels. If potassium supplementation is used, careful monitoring of the serum potassium level is necessary.
claims.locator: Contraindications › Antikaliuretic Therapy and Potassium Supplementation

claims.text: Hyperkalemia (≥5.5 mEq/L) is likelier with renal impairment, diabetes, and in the elderly or severely ill.
claims.quote: Abnormal elevation of serum potassium levels (≥5.5 mEq/liter) can occur with all potassium-sparing diuretic combinations, including triamterene and hydrochlorothiazide. Hyperkalemia is more likely to occur in patients with renal impairment and diabetes (even without evidence of renal impairment) and in the elderly or severely ill.
